newsitem.title: FRANCE: France expects wheat export jump after bumper crop.
newsitem.headline: France expects wheat export jump after bumper crop.

text.p: France produced a record wheat crop of 34.3 million tonnes this year, creating enough supply to nearly double its exports to developing countries, official estimates showed on Wednesday.
Cereals office ONIC said it had raised its crop estimate to 34.3 million tonnes from an earlier forecast of 33.8 million, breaking further ground above a 1984 record of 32.6 million.
It projected exports of soft wheat to countries outside the European Union of 6.8 million tonnes compared with a previous forecast of 6.7 million tonnes.
In 1995, France produced 29.8 million tonnes of soft wheat, and exported an unusually low 3.75 million tonnes, at a time when sales were under pressure from falling grain stocks.
In a published report, ONIC also raised its forecast for wheat exports to countries inside the 15-nation EU to 8.3 million tonnes from a previous 8.0 million.
Last season France sold 8.6 million tonnes to EU states.
Export figures apply to annual crop marketing seasons starting on July 1 each year.
The ONIC figures are the first since the French harvest was completed at the end of the summer and cofirm reports of unusually high grain yields this year despite drought in several regions.
But while the volume of wheat is up, millers say there are some doubts about supplies of the right quality of wheat for bread-making, containing adequate protein.
France is Europe's largest grain producer and exporter and usually a major supplier to world markets. Actual export levels depend on central EU policies controlled by the European Commission.

The EU, which also expects a bumper total wheat crop approaching 90 million tonnes this year, has said it expects to increase exports to world markets but will monitor the impact of this on domestic grain prices.
